tools.name: add_domain
tools.description: Connect a domain the person already owns to one of their sites (Pro plan). Returns the DNS records they must create at their domain provider. The domain starts serving once those records are in place and the certificate is issued, usually within minutes; use check_domain to follow it.

tools.name: add_editor
tools.description: Invite someone to edit a site you own: they can change its files, roll back and see its statistics, while you keep ownership (deleting it, domains, GitHub, editors). They get an email and become an editor when they accept.

tools.name: billing
tools.description: Get a link to subscribe to Hostlo Pro, or, for an account that already pays, to the billing page where the card, the invoices and cancelling live. Give the link to the person; nothing is charged until they finish on Stripe. Pro costs $7 a month or $70 a year (a founding price of $50 a year applies w

tools.name: check_domain
tools.description: Ask the certificate provider where a pending custom domain stands, and start serving it if it is ready.

tools.name: connect_repo
tools.description: Publish a site from a GitHub repository and republish it on every push. Works with private repositories. The first time, it returns a link the person opens to let Hostlo read their repositories; after they have, call it again. No builds are run: the folder is published as it is (found automatically,

tools.name: create_site
tools.description: Create a new site on a free subdomain. It stays empty until you publish files with write_files or start_upload. Before creating one, check what it is for against what Hostlo does not host (in the server instructions and /llms.txt), and tell the person first if it is not allowed.

tools.name: delete_files
tools.description: Delete files from a site and publish the result.

tools.name: delete_site
tools.description: Permanently delete a site, its files and its whole deploy history. The name becomes available to others.

tools.name: disconnect_repo
tools.description: Stop publishing a site from its GitHub repository. The site stays online with its current files, and can be edited here again. Pass the site name again in confirm.

tools.name: form_messages
tools.description: Read the messages people have sent through a site's contact form(s), newest first, shown with the form's own field labels. This is the inbox: use it when the person asks whether anyone has written in.

tools.name: import_site
tools.description: Copy an existing website (a WordPress site, a static site, or the Wayback Machine's saved copy of one) into a Hostlo site: its pages, styles, scripts, images and fonts, with links rewritten to work on Hostlo. Only import a site the person owns or has the right to copy, and ask them if that is not cl

tools.name: import_status
tools.description: How an import started with import_site is going, or its full report once finished: what was copied, what was left out and why.

tools.name: list_deploys
tools.description: Show a site's recent deploys, newest first, marking the live one.

tools.name: list_domains
tools.description: List the custom domains on this account, their status and what is still missing.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List the files of a site's live deploy with their sizes.

tools.name: list_forms
tools.description: List the contact forms on a site (or all your sites): their fields, where submissions go, and how many messages each has had.

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: List your sites with their public URLs, file counts and sizes.

tools.name: patch_file
tools.description: Edit a text file by exact search and replace, then publish. Each old_text must match exactly once.

tools.name: preferences
tools.description: Read or change the person's Hostlo preferences. Today that is the language of Hostlo's emails and web pages: English (en) or Khmer (km). Use it when they ask to read Hostlo in Khmer or English. Your own replies stay in whatever language you are speaking with them.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a text file from a site's live deploy.

tools.name: remove_domain
tools.description: Disconnect a custom domain. The site stays online at its Hostlo address. Pass the domain again in confirm.

tools.name: remove_editor
tools.description: Remove an editor from a site you own, or withdraw an invitation or handover offer sent to that address. An editor can also remove themselves (leave a site).

tools.name: remove_form
tools.description: Remove a contact form from a site. The stored messages are deleted with it. The HTML form on the page stops working; remove it from the page too.

tools.name: rename_site
tools.description: Rename a site you own. Its free address changes to the new name; the old address keeps working by redirecting to the new one, and the old name stays reserved for this site, so it can be switched back. Pages, history, statistics, custom domains, forms, editors and GitHub publishing all carry over. Co

tools.name: repo_status
tools.description: Show which sites are published from GitHub repositories: repository, branch, folder, the live commit, and why the last push failed if it did.

tools.name: rollback
tools.description: Make an earlier deploy live again. Nothing is deleted; you can roll forward the same way.

tools.name: set_form
tools.description: Add or update a contact form on a site. Describe the fields the visitor should fill (a name, an email, a message, a dropdown, and so on) and this stores them and returns an HTML form to drop into the page with write_files; the form posts to the site's own address, no third-party form service. tools.name: set_primary_domain
tools.description: Make one of a site's connected domains its main address. The site's other domains redirect visitors and search engines to this one, so only one copy is indexed. The domain must already be live (check_domain shows when it is). Use this when a site has more than one domain and the person says which sh

tools.name: site_members
tools.description: Who owns a site, who edits it, and which invitations or handover offers are waiting for an answer.

tools.name: site_stats
tools.description: Visitor statistics for a site: page views and unique visitors per day, top pages, referring sites and pages, visitors by country and which location served them. Counted without cookies or tracking scripts; recent views can take about a minute to appear.

tools.name: start_upload
tools.description: Prepare an upload of a local folder (for example a build output like dist/). Returns a one-time token and a shell command to run; only changed files are transferred. Valid for 60 minutes.

tools.name: transfer_site
tools.description: Hand a site over to someone else, for example a site made for a client. They get an email with a link; when they accept, the site is theirs (pages, history, statistics, custom domains) and counts against their plan. Ask whether the person wants to stay on as an editor (keep_me_as_editor), as an agen

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Show the signed-in account, its plan limits and usage, and the edge locations serving sites.

tools.name: write_files
tools.description: Create, replace and delete files in one deploy that goes live immediately. Use utf8 for text and base64 for small binary files. For large or many files use start_upload instead. Allowed: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, JSON, text, XML, SVG, web fonts, images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, ICO) and PDF; binary

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "list_files" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "read_file" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "set_form" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: add_editor, form_messages, list_forms, list_sites, preferences, transfer_site · Private data: add_domain, add_editor, connect_repo, create_site, delete_files, delete_site, disconnect_repo, form_messages, list_files, list_forms, list_sites, patch_file, read_file, remove_form, set_form, start_upload, write_files · Public sink: add_editor, connect_repo, create_site, delete_files, patch_file, rollback, set_form, start_upload, transfer_site · Destructive: connect_repo, delete_files, delete_site, remove_domain, remove_editor, remove_form, set_form, start_upload, write_files.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: add_editor, form_messages, list_forms, list_sites, preferences, transfer_site · Private data: add_domain, add_editor, connect_repo, create_site, delete_files, delete_site, disconnect_repo, form_messages, list_files, list_forms, list_sites, patch_file, read_file, remove_form, set_form, start_upload, write_files · Public sink: add_editor, connect_repo, create_site, delete_files, patch_file, rollback, set_form, start_upload, transfer_site · Destructive: connect_repo, delete_files, delete_site, remove_domain, remove_editor, remove_form, set_form, start_upload, write_files

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
